$comment: Hanse 508 geometry for sail-learn-and-train. Single source of truth for the 3D model and the rig solver. Units: metres and degrees. See docs/BOAT_REFERENCE.md for how every number was obtained and how confident we are.

meta.variant: Reference boat: in-mast furling main (manual, Selden, two-line furling drive), self-tacking jib on a Selden Furlex 404S manual furler, German mainsheet, rigid vang (Selden Rodkicker), single forestay, no gennaker rigged

frame.origin: Mast station (centre of mast section), on the waterline, on the centreline
frame.y: up is positive (y = 0 is the waterline)
frame.handedness: right-handed, matches three.js (x forward, y up, z starboard)

sourceKeys.brochure: Hanse 508 price list / spec sheet H508.22_PL_EN_20221216 (not stored in repo, copyrighted). Official figures.
sourceKeys.drawing: Measured from the brochure side view and deck plan drawings at ~35 px/m (side) and ~107 px/m (plan). Typical error +/-0.15 m.
sourceKeys.photo: Photos taken on the reference boat, stored in docs/reference/photos/.
sourceKeys.owner: Observed on board by the owner (stated directly).
sourceKeys.assumption: Engineering guess. Plausible but unverified. Safe to tune.
sourceKeys.manual: Hanse 508 owner's manual (German edition): official rig dimensions, masses, keel dimensions, running rigging table, mast-foot lead plan. Photographed by the owner; not stored (copyrighted). Takes priority over 'drawing'.

dimensions.rightingMomentSource: manual (heeling test, equipped boat). For Phase 2 heel.

deckEdgeHalfBeam.$comment: [x, half-beam] pairs traced from the deck plan outline, bow to stern. Max half-beam 2.375 = beam/2.

sheerHeight.$comment: [x, y] deck-edge height above the waterline. At the mast: manual (deck 1.96 m minus 0.39 m to the chainplates). Elsewhere: drawing, raised to match.

waterline.$comment: Hull meets the waterline from fwdX to aftX (difference = LWL 13.54). Plumb bow; the transom bottom sits just above the water.

canoeBody.$comment: Hull bottom (without keel). Deepest point and a smooth fair curve to the waterline ends is good enough.

keel.type: L-keel (cast iron fin with bulb extending aft)
keel.source: manual (Standard L-keel: F 1.96 top chord, H 2.61 bulb length, I 1.76 height, J 0.46 bulb width) + drawing (position)

rudder.topYNote: The hull bottom rises above the waterline aft of x = -7.34, so the rudder top meets the hull just above the waterline (as in the drawing).

saildrive.source: brochure + drawing (position) + manual (saildrive bottom 3.00 m below deck)

coachroof.maxHalfWidthSource: photo estimate (self-tacking-track-full.jpg: the track ends at the edges of the raised deck in front of the mast; track halfSpan 1.40)
coachroof.shapeNote: Plan: halfWidth (drawing) at aftX, widening in a straight taper to maxHalfWidth at maxHalfWidthFromX (the mast), full width from there to chamferStartX, then the corners are cut to frontHalfWidth at frontX. Side: the front face slopes from frontX at the deck back to topFrontX at the roof top. halfWidth, chamfer and front from the reference sketches; maxHalfWidth from the photo.
coachroof.topYSource: manual (deck 1.96 m above waterline at the mast)

aftPlatform.note: Teak aft deck over the fold-out bathing platform.

mast.source: manual (Hanse 508 owner's manual, German edition, rig and hull data pages; photographed by the owner, not stored in the repo)
mast.airDraftNote: Manual: mast 20.11 m from a deck 1.96 m above the waterline (sum 22.07); official 'mast height above WL approx. 22.05 m'. Tube top set to 22.04 so masthead fittings stay within the official figure.
mast.sectionSource: assumption (in-mast furling masts have a large section with a slot on the aft face)

spreaders.source: manual (Hanse 508 owner's manual, German edition, rig and hull data pages; photographed by the owner, not stored in the repo)
spreaders.note: Heights above the mast foot 6.15 m and 12.36 m. Spreader length measured along the spreader; sweep 24 deg. halfSpan = lateral reach = length x cos(sweep).

shrouds.source: manual (Hanse 508 owner's manual, German edition, rig and hull data pages; photographed by the owner, not stored in the repo)

chainplate.note: Cap shrouds: 2180 mm lateral, 865 mm aft of the mast centre; deck 390 mm above the chainplates

forestay.source: manual (Hanse 508 owner's manual, German edition, rig and hull data pages; photographed by the owner, not stored in the repo) (J 6.13 m from the mast front, FH 18.71 m above deck)

backstay.note: Drawn as a single backstay. Split or single on the reference boat: unknown.

boom.source: manual (Hanse 508 owner's manual, German edition, rig and hull data pages; photographed by the owner, not stored in the repo) (BH 1.51 m above deck)
boom.maxSwingSource: computed from the manual's chainplate position: the boom (half-thickness ~0.13 m) meets the cap shroud at about 72-73 deg

pitch.$comment: Boom pitch in degrees, + = boom end up. Phase-1 teaching approximation, prototyped in Python to satisfy PT-07/PT-08 smoothly. Tune visually, keep the tests green.
pitch.gravityDropNote: The rigid vang's gas spring holds the boom up against its own weight, so with no wind the boom only droops slightly. The mainsheet can still pull it lower.
pitch.toppingLiftNote: toppingLiftHauledDeg 4: below the vang's default limit (5 deg at 50 %), so at default settings a hauled topping lift visibly carries the boom; hauling both still makes them fight. toppingLiftEasedDeg -6: fully eased, the lift would let the boom end down to 6 deg below level, but the rigid vang strut stops it first (rig.vang.strutStopDeg), so an eased lift hangs slack with spare rope. The boom's lowest pitch is max(topping-lift limit, strut stop). Owner-approved assumptions (M2 review; separated from the strut stop after M2).

vang.type: Rigid vang: Selden Rodkicker (size 30) strut with a rope tackle. Pulls the boom down and its gas spring also supports it from below.
vang.render: Two telescoping tubes from the mast foot to the boom, with the tackle running alongside
vang.tacklePurchaseSource: assumption (rope tackle on the strut; the number of parts is not visible in the photo). Only changes the 'metres paid out' shown for the vang.
vang.strutStopSource: assumption, owner-approved (M2 review): the rigid vang strut stops the boom drooping more than about 2 deg below level, so a fully hauled main sheet cannot pull the boom end far down. Lowest boom pitch = max(topping-lift limit, strut stop).

toppingLift.source: photo (line from the boom end straight up the mast) + assumption (exit height)

outhaul.source: photo (two outhaul lines along the top of the boom: docs/reference/photos/mast-gooseneck-vang-outhaul.jpg) + assumption (block position)
outhaul.route: clew (comes out of the mast slot) -> one part aft along the top of the boom to a sheave at the boom end -> forward inside the boom (not drawn) -> out at the gooseneck -> down the mast -> turning block at the mast foot -> aft to clutch 'Main outhaul' (port bank)
outhaul.purchaseSource: unconfirmed (owner decision after M2: model 1:1, one part along the boom). The photo shows two lines at the clew, which could mean a 2:1 purchase. Moving the clew by 1 m needs 1 m of outhaul.

mainsheet.source: photo (both clutch banks carry MAIN SHEET) + drawing (positions)
mainsheet.system: German mainsheet: one rope, boom blocks <-> two deck blocks on the coachroof aft end, both tails led aft to the cockpit, no traveller
mainsheet.partsPerSideSource: photo: three blocks on the boom, two rope parts down to each spring-mounted deck block (docs/reference/photos/mainsheet-german.jpg)
mainsheet.routing: Boom blocks -> spring-mounted deck blocks on the coachroof aft end -> forward to the mast-foot lead organiser (port end at position 4, starboard end at position 7) -> aft in the coachroof channels -> clutch banks (manual lead plan + photos)

selfTackingTrack.source: photo (straight track right in front of the mast, spanning most of the deck width; docs/reference/photos/self-tacking-track-full.jpg) + drawing (position)
selfTackingTrack.shape: Straight athwartships track in plan view
selfTackingTrack.halfSpanSource: photo estimate (about 2.8 m end to end, ±0.3 m); the deck-plan drawing showed only about 1.8 m
selfTackingTrack.sheetBlockHeightSource: assumption: the jib sheet's block on the car sits this far above the track's centre line. The jib solver measures the sheet from the clew to this point, and the 3D car is drawn up to it (car height = this minus modelDetail.selfTackingTrack.radius), so the two always agree.

jibFurler.source: brochure (manual jib furler) + photo (Selden Furlex 404S) + drawing
jibFurler.lineTravelSource: assumption: metres of furling line that pass the JIB ROLL clutch between fully furled and fully unfurled (roughly 25 turns of a drum line of about 0.5 m). Only changes the 'metres paid out' shown for the jib furling line; capped at the 45 m in runningRigging.

mainFurlingGearbox.source: photo (Selden manual in-mast furling gearbox with winch-handle socket and IN/OUT arrow) + owner
mainFurlingGearbox.note: Two-line drive: one line furls (rolls the sail in), the other unfurls. Backup: turn the gearbox by hand with a winch handle at the mast. Exact height on the mast estimated. Photo shows it on a side face of the mast, below the gooseneck (which side: unconfirmed; port assumed).
mainFurlingGearbox.lineTravelSource: assumption: metres of furling line that pass the clutch between fully furled and fully unfurled (about 20 turns of a drum of about 0.13 m). Only changes the 'metres paid out' shown for the furling tails.

lineLead.source: manual (Selden 510-142 lead plan: lines turn at the mast-foot organiser and run aft) + photo (covered channels on the coachroof: mast-base-turning-blocks*.jpg, self-tacking-track-full.jpg) + assumption (exact path)
lineLead.$comment: Waypoints of the control lines between the mast foot and the clutch banks, starboard side; the port side is the mirror image (z negated). Each line runs a little apart from its neighbours (spacing, by clutch slot).
lineLead.mastExitNote: Where lines that run inside the mast (topping lift) or down its aft face (outhaul) leave it, above the furling gearbox.

mastFootLeadOrganiser.source: manual (Selden 510-142 lead plan, standard rig) + clutch photos
mastFootLeadOrganiser.note: Matches the clutch-bank sides: main halyard and jib sheet go to the starboard bank A. The plan is drawn for the standard (battened) rig; on our in-mast boat the reef positions carry the furling lines, and the bank labels win where they differ.

main.source: manual (Hanse 508 owner's manual, German edition, rig and hull data pages; photographed by the owner, not stored in the repo)
main.areaNote: Triangle P x E / 2 = 56.4 m2; the manual's 61 m2 includes some roach. Fine for teaching.
main.furl: Rolls into the mast. Unfurled fraction f moves the clew along the boom: clewDistance = f * footLength. Luff stays full height.

jib.source: manual (Hanse 508 owner's manual, German edition, rig and hull data pages; photographed by the owner, not stored in the repo) (luff on the forestay, LP 5.26 m, area 51.5 m2)
jib.type: Self-tacking jib on a manual furler
jib.clewTrimmedRefNote: Clew fully trimmed with the car at the starboard end of the track (wind from port). Mirror z for the other tack.
jib.furl: Rolls around the forestay. Unfurled fraction f: foot and leech shrink towards the luff; the clew moves forward along the foot direction.

sheet.hauledClewToCarNote: Sanity reference only. Fully hauled, the jib sits with the car just at the end of the track (about 14 deg out; the track ends set how far in a self-tacking jib can be pulled). The app computes this clew-car length from geometry at startup (about 0.53 m to the car's sheet block, rig.selfTackingTrack.sheetBlockHeight). Changed after the M3 review: before, fully hauled meant the jib on the centreline.
sheet.purchaseSource: photo: two rope parts between the clew and the car
sheet.route: car -> along the track -> turning block at the mast foot -> aft along the coachroof -> clutch 'Genoa sheet' (starboard bank)
sheet.maxEaseBeyondHauledNote: Working length added between fully hauled and fully eased. Retuned after the M3 review (was 1.6 m beyond the centred clew) so a fully eased jib still opens to about 31 deg (PT-11).
sheet.releasedNote: Owner decision after M3: at this setting the sheet counts as released for furling. Its working length is then max(the sailing length above, the clew-car length the furl needs to keep the jib at its fully-out angle), so the jib furls completely, keeps its angle and flaps (M3 review: it is no longer pulled in to the centreline). A fully unfurled jib uses the sailing length, so sailing (PT-11) is unchanged. Below it, furling stops where the sheet is too short (PT-13).

gennaker.note: Exists as a brochure option (176.4 m2, own halyard and 2 sheets). Not rigged on the reference boat. Data slot reserved; implement in a later phase behind a settings toggle.

reacher.note: Option on a second forestay (87.4 m2, genoa tracks). Not on the reference boat as far as known.

cockpitHardware.source: drawing (positions), photo (labels, layout), owner (which bank is on which side)

winches.note: Standard: 2 x Lewmar 55 ST EVO (brochure). Photo: one winch per side next to the wheel, aft of the clutch bank.
Option XC5200 drawn on the deck plan. Not on the reference boat (photo shows one winch per side). Do not render.

clutchBanks.sideSource: owner (the main furling lines are on the right side)

clutches.label: Main furling
clutches.tailNote: Left of the two: rolls the main in (owner confirmed the right one unfurls)

clutches.label: Main furling
clutches.tailNote: Right of the two: rolls the main out (owner)

clutchBanks.sideSource: owner (the vang is on the left side)

jibRollClutch.label: JIB ROLL
jibRollClutch.source: photo: on the port side deck next to the sprayhood, the furling line runs forward along the stanchion bases to the bow (fore-aft position estimated)

engineControl.type: Single-lever throttle/gear control (Allpa) with start/stop/power panel and tachometer

helmInstruments.note: Photo of the starboard helm: magnetic compass, B&G multifunction display and B&G autopilot control next to the winch; rope tails stowed in a bin at the helm. Phase 2+.

mastBase.note: All halyards and control lines come down the mast and turn at a ring of Selden turning blocks at the mast foot, then run aft along the coachroof in covered channels, one group to each clutch bank. Photos: mast-base-turning-blocks*.jpg.

ropes.$comment: Every rope the model knows. 'path' lists fitting/point ids from the working end to the tail; the renderer draws straight segments between them, except the 'working' segment which can sag. Static ropes are drawn but not controllable in Phase 1.

list.working: tackle along the rigid vang strut, mast foot <-> boom
one part along the top of the boom from the sail clew (at the mast slot) to a sheave at the boom end, then forward inside the boom to the mast
list.coupled: hauled together with the unfurl tail, against the furl tail

list.working: mast gearbox drum -> aft; two tails: one furls, the other unfurls
furler drum -> aft along the port side deck via stanchion-base fairleads

list.note: With in-mast furling the main halyard stays hoisted.
Parked. Belongs to the gennaker (not rigged).

controls.$comment: All rope controls are continuous 0..100 with a user-selectable step (1% or 5%). Convention: 0 = fully hauled in / furled, 100 = fully eased / unfurled.

clutchPanel.$comment: Ropes tab (PHASE1_SPEC 7.2, M4a): facts the clutch-bank drawing needs. Which clutch holds which rope, and the labels, are in cockpitHardware. Sizes of the drawing itself are presentation and live in src/ui/clutchDrawing.ts.
clutchPanel.largeClutchSource: photo: the two halyard clutches are a bigger type with a lever on top (clutch-bank-a.jpg, clutch-bank-b.jpg)
clutchPanel.staticRopeNotesComment: Why a rope has no control in Phase 1; the UI shows the matching text (ropes.static.*).

steering.$comment: Wheel and rudder (PHASE1_SPEC 4, 7.1). Visual only in Phase 1. Range and default: controls.list ctl_rudder; wheel turns: cockpitHardware.wheelTurnsLockToLock.
steering.rudderSign: ctl_rudder > 0: the rudder's back edge to starboard. The wheel is turned clockwise (seen from behind it, facing forward) and the boat would turn to starboard, as a car does.

modelDetail.$comment: Sizes of small parts that only the 3D model needs (thicknesses, diameters, section shapes). Not measured: chosen to look right and be tappable at teaching scale. They do not affect the rig solver. Safe to tune.
modelDetail.hullSectionExponentNote: Cross-section shape of the hull between the keel line and the deck edge (superellipse). 2 = round bilge, higher = fuller, flatter bottom and more upright topsides.
modelDetail.wireRenderRadiusNote: Shrouds and stays drawn thicker than real (about 12-16 mm) so they stay visible on a phone, like visual.ropeRenderRadius.
modelDetail.rudderBalanceNote: Fraction of the rudder chord in front of the stock (balanced spade rudder).
modelDetail.mainsheetBoomBlockSpacingNote: Three blocks under the boom (photo), centred on rig.mainsheet.boomDistance; spacing estimated.
modelDetail.vangTackleOffsetNote: The vang tackle is drawn this far beside the strut so both stay visible.
modelDetail.outhaulPartSpacingNote: The outhaul is drawn this far to port of the boom's centre line on top of the boom, clear of the topping lift.
modelDetail.jibSheetPartSpacingNote: The jib sheet's two parts between the clew and the car are drawn this far apart so both stay visible.
modelDetail.vangStrutNote: Rigid vang drawn as two telescoping tubes: the thick one from the mast point, the thin one from the boom point, each tubeFraction of the strut length at rest so they overlap.
modelDetail.mastBaseTurningBlocksNote: Ring of turning blocks around the mast foot (photos mast-base-turning-blocks*.jpg); count and sizes estimated.
modelDetail.sprayhoodNote: Fabric shelter on the aft end of the coachroof over the companionway; its aft edge is at the coachroof's aft end. Size and position estimated from photos (side-deck-jib-roll.jpg, mainsheet-german.jpg).
modelDetail.lifelinesNote: Stanchions along both deck edges with an upper and a lower wire (photo side-deck-jib-roll.jpg); positions and heights estimated.

visual.$comment: Teaching approximations for Phase 1. Not physics. Tune freely, keep them here.
visual.jibCarMiddleNote: Closer than this to the middle of its track, the panel says the car is in the middle.
visual.jibWindShadowNote: With the wind at least this far aft, the panel adds that on a run the mainsail blocks the jib's wind (Phase 2 models it; M3 review).
visual.boomSmoothingNote: Time constant of the critically damped spring that moves the drawn boom towards the solved pose (PHASE1_SPEC 8.3 step 5). The fill of the sails follows with the same time constant.
visual.gybeSwingNote: Faster spring while the boom swings across in an accidental gybe.

solver.furledNote: Below this much mainsail out there is no sail to push or lift the boom (PT-14); the sail is not drawn either.

mainSail.$comment: Look of the mainsail mesh (PHASE1_SPEC 8.6). camberRatio: depth of the curve as a fraction of the chord when filled. The luff ripple is the flapping of a luffing sail: amplitude at referenceKn, scaled with the wind speed, strongest at the luff.

runningRigging.source: manual (running rigging table, option FCL = in-mast furling). The charter boat's actual ropes may differ (photos show white ropes with blue or black flecks).

rope_jib_furling_line.note: Assumed to be the 'Vorlaeufer' (10 mm, 45 m) in the table; unconfirmed

runningRigging.use: Total rope lengths are upper limits for paid-out length; diameters can scale the rendered thickness.
